title: fix: distinguish fallback spillover from degradation
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds `primary_5xx`, `primary_retried_503s`, and `fallback_rescues` to `model_health`.
- Keeps DEGRADED based only on final user-visible outcomes.
- Reports non-final primary 503 pressure separately as SPILLOVER.
- Preserves the current hide/relist monitor workflow and community rate-limit exclusions.

Root cause: the image-specific monitor query counted non-final Z-Image Vast 503 attempts even when Fal handled the final response.

Checks:
- `git diff --check`
- Proposed Tinybird SQL executed against live data: final 5xx remained zero while retried primary 503s were reported separately

Tinybird has not been deployed. Rollout: validate/deploy staging, merge, deploy production, then verify the monitor auto-refreshes from `main` on its next cycle.

gist.headline: Spillover is not a wilted flower
gist.blurb: The monitor learned the difference between a rough first landing and a failed delivery. When Fal rescues an image request after a primary 503, the hive now records the detour without declaring the whole flowerbed degraded.
gist.summary: Updated the model-health Tinybird query to track `primary_5xx`, `primary_retried_503s`, and `fallback_rescues`, keeping DEGRADED status tied only to final user-visible failures while exposing retried primary 503 pressure as SPILLOVER.
gist.impact: Models whose Z-Image Vast requests receive a non-final 503 before Fal returns a successful final image can remain correctly listed as healthy, while operators still see the underlying primary-provider spillover separately.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy garden delivery route: a primary watering pipe briefly sputters with a small pixel “503” sign, while a friendly backup pipe successfully waters the code-plant. Polli calmly checks a health clipboard showing separate HEALTHY and SPILLOVER indicators, emphasizing that a rescued request is not the same as a failed one.
